original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Price a changed schedule that co-hosts present-head flag 43's basis head (15) in the target Y59 at a target update while the source X21 still hosts it and is still live, answering open question 1 of #3456 (and the matching question of #3451/#3443 for this flag). Construct the repair as an explicit splice of the published #1991 word, run the published p104-native-channel validate() on the repaired word with eight newly lowered native edges, and give the exact before/after bill (events, ADDs, transport occurrences, rank mass, paid H_r profile, native edges). Add the matching obstruction: in the class that keeps the published event order and ADDs, keeps endpoint frames and adds no rank mass, event 3364 is the only Y59 update that can be made head-hosting, and it forces exactly Y59, D17, Y103 and D28 to change.
scope_change_reason: #3451, #3456 and #3443 prove the published word never co-hosts the basis head at a target update on flags 1, 43 and 9, and leave pricing a repair open. This package does not re-derive those chronologies; it cites them and adds the repair, its native validation, its bill and a forced-closure obstruction for flag 43. Flag 43 was chosen because #3456 records that its last target chart is one rank step from the head and names the D17 common-chart constraint.
bottleneck_link: The present-head obstruction on flag 43 is a scheduling artefact, not a cost barrier: the head can be co-hosted at the target update that settles X21's final coefficient without adding any event, ADD, transport or rank unit to the published channel. The remaining cost is a rank-profile reshuffle that is free under any affine per-rank price and weakly favourable under any convex one. This does not supply I-G/2, a side correction or a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after one flag (43): one event-preserving repair R0 and one order-changing comparison R1, both natively validated and billed, plus the forced-hosting closure of every Y59 update. Do not touch flags 0, 1 or 9, recompute relay coefficients beyond the X21 entries of Y59, or build a side correction.
evidence: R0 retargets nine published transports (3362, 3363, 3365, 3460, 3461, 3525, 3569, 3612, 3634) and relabels three ADD charts (3364, 3366, 3462); every changed frame is its published frame plus 15. The published check_native.validate() passes on the repaired word: 740 native edges (8 swapped for 8 newly lowered), 208 endpoint adapters, all 280 framed rows and 72 dirty helpers restored. Bill: 4058 events, 2624 ADDs, 1410 transport occurrences and rank mass 2368, all unchanged; paid profile {1:1074,2:58,3:86,4:104} becomes {1:1071,2:63,3:85,4:103}, delta -3H1+5H2-H3-H4; the nine changed ranks {4,3,3,2,1,1,1,1,1} become {3,2,2,2,2,2,2,1,1}, which the published multiset majorizes. In R0 the last Y59 update (3364, D17, coefficient 1/4) runs in chart [95,447,6,32,20,15] while X21 is at the rank-9 full chart with four later reads; that ADD carries X21 coefficient 1/2 and settles Y59's final X21 coefficient 1/2 (after +1/2 at 3076 and -1/2 at 3231). R1 instead moves Y103's 3365-3366 before Y59's update and gives D17 one added rank-1 transport: +1 event, +1 transport occurrence, rank mass unchanged, delta +2H2-H4, 742 native edges. Forced closure on the published word: 14 of 15 Y59 updates force the head into a register whose final frame excludes it (first: Y67, Y96, Y26, Y56 or Y22); only 3364 is admissible, forcing D17 at 3364, Y103 at 3366 and D28 at 3462. All 280 non-private registers sit at their rank floor, so zero added rank mass means monotone paths. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Does the same head-step repair exist for present-head flags 1 and 9, and what is the forced closure of their target updates?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If every present-head flag admits an event-preserving repair, the present-head obstruction recorded by #3451/#3443/#3456 is uniformly a scheduling artefact; a flag whose closure is obstructed would instead need added rank or a reordering, with a priced floor.
open_questions.first_step: Run this package's closure_table on Y7 (flag 1, head 232) and Y23 (flag 9, head 196) as a separate package citing #3451 and #3443, without re-certifying their chronologies.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package treats flag 43 only. Flags 1 and 9 are the subjects of open #3451 and #3443.

open_questions.question: Can a correction program use the co-hosted head chart at 3364 to restore X21's contribution to Y59 dirtily, and what does the I-G/2 side correction then cost at that cut?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 removes the geometric reason given by #3456 for why chronological dirty restoration cannot use co-hosted head geometry on flag 43. Whether the side correction can exploit it is the actual supplier question.
open_questions.first_step: At R0's event 3364, price one added X21-to-Y59 transfer in the common head chart (both registers would need a shared frame; X21 is at the full chart) against the channel's existing allowance.
open_questions.blocked_by: No side-correction word is built here; the channel still implements G/2, not I.

open_questions.question: Is R0's rank profile optimal among event-preserving monotone repairs under every convex per-rank price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 uses the minimal admissible frame at each forced event, but a different choice of intermediate frames could give a profile that the R0 profile does not majorize.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the admissible frames for the nine forced transports inside each register's final span and compare the resulting rank multisets by majorization.
